title: Learning from a stream
sub: Predict, see the label, update. Then the world changes.

frames.caption: Points arrive one at a time; blue is class +1, orange is −1. The perceptron predicts each one with its current line (solid), then updates only if it was wrong. The dashed line is the true boundary, which it never sees.
Mistake: w ← w + y·x. The weight vector (arrow) swings towards a misclassified +1, or away from a misclassified −1, and the line, which is perpendicular to it, rotates.
Large dots mark the examples it got wrong. Correctly predicted points cause no update at all.
Each mistake nudges the line closer to the truth, and mistakes become rarer.
After a handful of updates the line separates the stream well.

10 mistakes in 300 examples, the last at example 160. Novikoff's theorem guarantees at most (R/γ)² mistakes on any separable stream, where R is the largest |x| and γ the margin: here (1.39 / 0.10)² ≈ 192. The bound is loose, but it holds no matter how adversarial the order.

A stream where the true boundary is fixed... for now. Three logistic regression models learn by SGD; each curve is accuracy over the last 100 predictions, measured before the model sees each label. All three have learned the concept.
At t = 600 the concept changes suddenly: the true boundary rotates by 90°. Same inputs, different labels. This is concept drift: p(y | x) changed.

Accuracy drops for all three. Grey was frozen at the drift, as if it were deployed from a batch job. Orange uses a learning rate that decays like 1/t, as convergence theory recommends for a fixed distribution. Blue keeps a constant learning rate.
Blue recovers within about a hundred examples. Orange recovers, but slowly: by t = 600 its steps had already shrunk, so 600 old examples outvote the new ones. Grey never recovers.

Final rolling accuracy: constant rate 99%, decaying rate 76%, frozen 54%. A constant learning rate weights recent examples more heavily, exponentially forgetting old ones. That is exactly what you want under drift, and exactly what you don't want on a fixed distribution, where it keeps the model noisy.
